title: F First Word
statementMd:
First Word
     Input file:            standard input
     Output file:           standard output
     Time limit:            5 seconds
     Memory limit:          1024 megabytes

VegiCat has a string S of n lowercase English letters. He wants to build a dictionary that contains k
distinct nonempty substrings of S as its words. A substring is a contiguous part of a string. Substrings
with the same content are treated as the same word, even if they occur at different positions in S.
Let π be a mapping from the letters a, b, . . . , z to the corresponding letters in a permutation of the
26 lowercase English letters. For example, the permutation qwertyuiopasdfghjklzxcvbnm defines the
following mapping:

                        c a b c d e f g h i j k l m n o p q r s t u v w x y z
                       π(c) q w e r t y u i o p a s d f g h j k l z x c v b n m

For a string u = u1 u2 · · · um , define

                                           π(u) = π(u1 )π(u2 ) · · · π(um ).

For example, with the mapping above, π(apple) = qhhst.
VegiCat wants the dictionary to contain a word w such that, after applying any such mapping π to every
word in the dictionary, π(w) is always the lexicographically smallest word in the resulting dictionary.
For each k = 1, 2, . . . , n, find the number of dictionaries that contain k distinct words and satisfy the
requirement, modulo 998244353.
Two dictionaries are considered different if and only if they contain different sets of words before any
mapping is applied.
Recall that string a is lexicographically smaller than string b if a is a prefix of b (and a ̸= b), or there
exists an index i (1 ≤ i ≤ min(|a|, |b|)) such that ai < bi , and for any index j (1 ≤ j < i) aj = bj .

Input
The first line contains an integer T (1 ≤ T ≤ 104 ), the number of test cases. The description of the test
cases follows.
The first line of each test case contains an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 105 ).
The second line contains a string S of length n, consisting only of lowercase English letters.
It is guaranteed that the sum of n over all test cases does not exceed 105 .

Output
For each test case, output n integers on one line. The k-th integer represents the number of dictionaries
that contain k distinct words and satisfy the requirement, modulo 998244353.

Example
                 standard input                                   standard output
 3                                                     5 4 3
 3                                                     8 10 11 10
 aab                                                   21 52 87 119 139 128 84
 4
 ppqq
 7
 abcaabc

 Note
Each dictionary below is written as a set of words.
For the first test case, S = aab, the dictionaries that satisfy the requirement for k = 1, 2, 3 are:

                  k   Word sets that satisfy the requirement  Number of dictionaries
                  1   {a}, {b}, {aa}, {ab}, {aab}                      5
                  2   {a, aa}, {a, ab}, {a, aab}, {aa, aab}            4
                  3   {a, aa, ab}, {a, aa, aab}, {a, ab, aab}          3
